*[[Syrian civil war]]

***A [[car bomb]]ing kills at least seven people and injures another ten in [[Ras al-Ayn]], [[al-Hasakah Governorate]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1740446/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
*[[Islamic terrorism in Europe]], [[terrorism in France]]
**The suspect in the stabbing attack yesterday outside the former headquarters of the satirical magazine ''[[Charlie Hebdo]]'' in [[Paris]] is identified as Ali H., an 18-year-old [[Pakistan]]-born man. He confessed to his actions and said he acted in vengeance for the magazine's [[Muhammad]] [[caricature]] republications earlier this year. [https://www.lci.fr/police/il-assume-son-acte-qui-est-ali-h-l-auteur-presume-de-l-attaque-a-paris-pres-des-anciens-locaux-e-charlie-hebdo-2165577.html (LCI)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-europe-54307820 (BBC News)]
*[[Boko Haram insurgency]]
**Eleven people are killed and 13 others injured after [[Boko Haram]] militants attack a security convoy taking people [[forced displacement|displaced]] by an [[insurgency]] back to their homes in [[Borno State]], [[Nigeria]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-nigeria-security/suspected-islamists-kill-at-least-11-in-attack-on-convoy-in-northeast-nigeria-idUSKBN26H0TJ (Reuters)]
*Security forces kill at least nine insurgents in [[Lebanon]] during operations against [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]-linked militants that killed four security forces earlier this month and three civilians in August. Three security forces are also injured in this incident. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1740741/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
*Militants open fire on an army checkpoint in Araman, [[Lebanon]], killing two members of the security forces. A militant is also killed in the attack. It is the third of a spate of attacks by [[Islamic State of Iraq and the Levant|Islamic State]]-linked militants in the country since August. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-lebanon-security/lebanese-security-forces-kill-two-members-of-armed-group-sources-say-idUSKBN26H0VF (Reuters)]
*Militants kill at least 15 people in [[Ethiopia]]'s western [[Benishangul-Gumuz Region]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-ethiopia-violence/armed-militia-kills-at-least-15-people-in-western-ethiopia-idUSKBN26H0CD (Reuters)]

***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Kingdom]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Scotland]]
*****[[Scotland]] reports 714 new cases, the biggest single-day jump on record since the [[COVID-19 pandemic|pandemic]] began. It amounts to 11.5% of newly-tested individuals, the highest proportion of positivity rate tests. [https://news.stv.tv/scotland/coronavirus-scotland-records-714-new-cases-overnight?top&amp (STV)]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Ireland]]
*****[[Northern Ireland]] reports 319 new cases in the past 24 hours, setting a new record for the second consecutive day. The previous record was reported yesterday with 273 cases. [https://www.belfasttelegraph.co.uk/news/health/coronavirus/coronavirus-northern-ireland-one-further-death-reported-as-new-covid-19-cases-hit-record-319-39564326.html (''The Belfast Telegraph'')]

;Politics
*[[2020–2021 United States racial unrest]], [[George Floyd protests in Portland, Oregon|George Floyd protests in Portland]]
**[[Governor of Oregon]] [[Kate Brown]] declares a weekend [[state of emergency]] for [[Portland, Oregon|Portland]], saying [[white supremacy|white supremacist groups]] are travelling from out of state to attend an event the [[Proud Boys]] allege to be organized to "end domestic terrorism." Thousands of supporters are expected as police prepare for clashes in a city that has become the center of sometimes deadly political violence in the run-up to the [[2020 United States presidential election|November 3 election]]. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/portland-proud-boys-rally-state-of-emergency-1.5740450 (CBC)]
